questions.stem: Sarah had 55 cards. She gave 20% of them to her sister, 25% of the remaining to her brother, and the rest to her best friend. What percentage of the cards did she give to her best friend?
questions.hint: Work out how many cards are left after each gift, then convert the final leftover amount to a percentage of the original 55.

steps.explain: Find 20% of the original 55 cards, given to her sister, then find how many remain.
steps.work: 20\% \text{ of } 55 = 11 \implies 55 - 11 = 44 \text{ left}

steps.explain: Find 25% of the 44 remaining cards, given to her brother, then find how many remain.
steps.work: 25\% \text{ of } 44 = 11 \implies 44 - 11 = 33 \text{ left}

steps.explain: The 33 leftover cards go to her best friend. Express 33 as a percentage of the ORIGINAL 55, not of 44 — that is the key pitfall in this question.
steps.work: \dfrac{33}{55} \times 100 = \dfrac{3}{5} \times 100 = 60

steps.explain: Pitfall: a very common mistake is to compute 33 as a percentage of 44 instead of the original 55, giving 75% (option C); forgetting the second gift entirely and reporting the 44 left after just the first gift as a percentage of 55 gives 80% (option D); wrongly adding the two given percentages (20%+25%=45%) and subtracting from 100% gives 55% (option A) — this ignores that the 25% is of the REMAINING amount, not the original.
steps.work: \text{Answer: } 60\%
